label: D1 after an unrewarded trial, first half of episode
explanation: Fires only at D1 steps and only when the reward input shows the previous trial was unrewarded (prev_reward == 0). It never fires at GO or D2, after a rewarded trial, or on the first trial of the episode. Activation fades with episode time: firing rate is about 0.12 in trials 0-49, falls quickly after trial 50, and is roughly zero after trial 75. The ep_trial < 55 cutoff gives the best F1; lower-magnitude activations make up most of what this predicate misses, and they sit in later trials. Magnitude is somewhat higher when the trial two back was rewarded (the first omission after a reward). In top windows it goes 1.0, then about 0.72, then about 0.58 over consecutive unrewarded D1s. Every variable used is observed (the reward input and elapsed time), so no future variables are involved. Without the time condition, prev_reward==0 at D1 alone gives recall 1.0 but precision 0.52.

issues: All the factual claims hold on the dev profile. Activity is 100% at D1, with zero activations at GO and D2. There are zero activations when prev_reward == 1. ep_bucket 0 (the episode's first trial) has zero activations. Firing decays with episode time: rates by 10-trial bin are 0.125, 0.114, 0.114, 0.110, 0.093, 0.052, 0.022, 0.004, 0.000, 0.000.
The '~0.12 firing rate in trials 0-49' figure is the rate over all steps, not the rate among D1s after an omission, which is much higher. The wording is loose, but the claim isn't wrong.
Test scores reproduce: precision 0.905, recall 0.919, F1 0.912, mass recall 0.977. With no time condition, the predicate gets precision 0.524 and recall 1.000, matching the claim.

The misses on test hold only 2.3% of activation mass, and the predicate covers 75% of steps even in the lowest activation quartile. They are low-magnitude D1-after-omission activations past trial 55, plus a few tiny ones near the boundary. That is the stated time decay, not a separate class.

The false positives cluster in trials 30-55 (precision 0.81 there vs 0.99 for trials under 30) and in long losing streaks (precision 0.75 when trials -2 and -3 were also unrewarded). This matches the stated decline in magnitude over consecutive omissions; it is a matter of degree, not a new pattern.

There is a mild asymmetry by previous action: precision is 0.95 after a2 vs 0.85 after a1. Giving each action its own time cutoff only raises test F1 from 0.912 to 0.919, so it isn't a meaningful systematic gap.
Splitting by rare vs common transition on the previous trial gives no clean class: precision is 0.88 for rare and 0.93 for common. The predicate uses no future variables.
